records.text: Binary Search Tree Iterator (lazy inorder traversal)
key_points: Perform an in‑order traversal lazily using a stack that stores the path to the next smallest node.
Constructor: push all left descendants of root onto the stack – O(h) time, h = tree height.
next(): pop top node, push its right child's leftmost chain – O(average 1) amortized, O(h) worst case.
hasNext(): simply check if stack is non‑empty – O(1).
Space is O(h) for the stack; handles degenerate trees (h = n) and empty tree edge cases.

records.text: Memory-efficient ProRAW image decoder. Category: Systems (ICT4). Description: Decode for iOS devices with <=1GB RAM.
key_points: Read the ProRAW file in small, fixed‑size chunks (e.g., 4 KB) to keep peak memory < 1 GB.
Use a streaming decoder (e.g., libjpeg‑turbo or custom CFA demosaic) that processes each chunk and writes the resulting RGB pixels directly to a memory‑mapped output buffer or file.
Avoid loading the whole raw sensor array; keep only a sliding window of rows needed for demosaicing (typically 2‑3 rows).
Complexity: O(N) time where N is number of pixels; O(W) auxiliary space where W is the width of the image (row buffer).
Edge cases: images with non‑standard Bayer patterns, corrupted headers, and handling of 16‑bit vs 12‑bit raw data.

records.text: Lock-free queue for real-time watchOS sensor data. Category: Concurrency (ICT4). Description: Lock-free implementation.
key_points: Implement a lock‑free circular buffer using atomic head and tail indices (e.g., std::atomic<size_t>).
Producers write at head index with compare‑exchange; consumers read from tail index similarly, ensuring wrap‑around with modulo buffer size.
Use memory_order_acquire/release to guarantee visibility of written data without locks.
Time per operation is O(1) with only a few atomic instructions; space is a fixed-size ring buffer sized for worst‑case sensor burst.
Edge cases: buffer full (drop or overwrite policy), wrap‑around race when head catches up to tail, and handling of 64‑bit counters to avoid ABA problem.

records.text: Debug a PyTorch U-Net shape mismatch. Category: ML Debugging. Description: ML Engineer round.
key_points: Identify the mismatched tensor shapes by printing shapes of each intermediate tensor in the U‑Net forward pass.

Typical cause: concatenation of encoder feature map with upsampled decoder map where spatial dimensions differ due to padding/stride; fix by using `torch.nn.functional.interpolate` or `torch.nn.ConvTranspose2d` with appropriate output_padding.
Ensure all Conv2d layers use `padding = kernel_size // 2` to keep dimensions constant when needed.
After alignment, verify that batch size and channel dimensions match before each concat – O(1) runtime impact.
Edge cases: odd input dimensions causing off‑by‑one size, mismatched number of channels, and using `nn.ModuleList` vs plain list which can affect parameter registration.

records.text: Bag-of-Words similarity search. Category: ML Coding. Description: ML Engineer round.
key_points: Convert each document to a sparse term‑frequency vector; optionally apply TF‑IDF weighting.
Compute cosine similarity between query vector and each document: similarity = (A·B) / (||A||·||B||).
Use a vectorizer like `sklearn.feature_extraction.text.CountVectorizer` or `TfidfVectorizer` for O(N·L) preprocessing (N docs, L avg length).
For fast retrieval, build an inverted index mapping terms to posting lists; then compute similarity only on candidate docs (sparse dot product).
Complexities: preprocessing O(N·L), query O(#unique terms in query × avg posting length); space O(V + total non‑zero entries). Edge cases: empty query, unseen terms, and very high‑dimensional vocab.

records.text: Find Minimum Processing Rate. Category: Binary Search. Description: Koko-style binary search on answer (ML Engineer).
key_points: Binary search on the answer space: low = 1, high = max(piles) (or total/k).
For a candidate rate mid, compute hours needed = Σ ceil(pile / mid); if hours ≤ H, rate is sufficient → move high = mid‑1, else low = mid+1.
Time complexity O(N log M) where N = number of piles, M = max pile size; space O(1).
Edge cases: H < number of piles (impossible → answer = max pile), H == N (rate = max pile), and piles with size 0.
Return low as the minimal feasible processing rate.

records.text: Minimum Cells to Bridge a Magic Grid. Category: Graph / BFS. Description: Islands/bridging grid hard.
key_points: Treat each island (connected component of 1s) as a node; compute all‑pairs shortest bridge lengths via BFS from every island’s perimeter.
Use multi‑source BFS: enqueue all border cells of each island with its island id and distance 0; when two fronts meet, bridge length = dist1 + dist2.
Keep a min‑heap of candidate bridges; apply Kruskal’s algorithm (Union‑Find) to select minimum set that connects all islands.
Time complexity O(R·C) for BFS + O(E log E) for Kruskal, where E is number of candidate bridges; space O(R·C) for visited/dist arrays.
Edge cases: single island (answer 0), isolated islands with no possible bridge (grid edges), and handling of diagonal adjacency if not allowed.

records.text: Library Management System. Category: OOP Design. Description: Actual class structure expected.
key_points: Core classes: `Library`, `Book`, `Member`, `Loan`, and `Catalog` (for search).
`Library` aggregates collections of `Book` and `Member`; provides methods `checkout(memberId, isbn)`, `returnBook(memberId, isbn)`, and `searchByTitle/Author` delegating to `Catalog`.
`Book` holds ISBN, title, author, copy count, and a list of current `Loan`s; `Member` tracks memberId, contact info, and a list of active loans.
`Loan` records `book`, `member`, `checkoutDate`, `dueDate`; implements overdue check logic.

Design uses composition (Library has Catalog) and encapsulation; interfaces allow swapping persistence layers (in‑memory vs DB). Edge cases: trying to checkout when no copies available, returning a book not loaned, and member exceeding loan limit.

records.text: AI agents for test coverage: design discussion on hallucination handling, oversight, and failure monitoring. Category: AI Round (IC3). Description: Ran as a whiteboard design conversation in at least one 2026 loop; no live prompting required.
key_points: Use a layered architecture: LLM core, deterministic validation layer, and monitoring/oversight service.
Detect hallucinations by cross‑checking LLM outputs against a knowledge base or using a secondary verification model; fallback to human review when confidence is low.
Implement failure monitoring with metrics (error rate, latency, coverage gaps) and alerts; store execution traces for post‑mortem.
Design a feedback loop: flagged outputs trigger model fine‑tuning or rule updates, and the system can automatically retry with stricter constraints.
Discuss scalability: stateless LLM workers behind a load balancer, shared cache for test artifacts, and eventual consistency for coverage metrics.

records.text: Time-to-live token manager with renewal. Category: Concurrency / Design (tech screen, Sep 2026). Description: generate, renew (only while unexpired) and count_unexpired, expiry wins ties at the same timestamp; part 2 makes it thread-safe under heavy concurrent reads and writes. Interviewer framed it around an LLM application.
key_points: Core data structure: a concurrent hash map keyed by token ID storing (expiryTime, version) plus a min‑heap (or TreeMap) ordered by expiry for O(log n) cleanup.
generate: O(1) insert; renew: check current time < expiry, then update expiry and heap entry (O(log n)).
count_unexpired: purge expired entries from the heap up to current time (amortized O(k log n)) then return map size; O(1) if lazy cleanup.
Thread safety: use a read‑write lock or java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap with synchronized heap updates; atomic compare‑and‑set for renew to avoid race conditions.

records.text: First successful result from parallel API calls under a global timeout. Category: Concurrency (tech screen, Sep 2026). Description: Start all slow, failure-prone calls at once, return the first success, one deadline across all waits, tell "all failed" from "timed out", cancel in-flight work; follow-ups on hedged requests and capping concurrency at k.
key_points: Launch all API calls as separate async tasks (e.g., CompletableFuture or goroutine) and attach a shared deadline timer.
Use a select/await‑any pattern: the first task that completes successfully signals the main thread; failures are collected until either a success or the global timeout expires.

Distinguish timeout vs all‑failed by tracking whether the deadline fired before any success; if deadline passes and no success, return timeout error; if all tasks finish with errors before deadline, return all‑failed.
Cancel remaining in‑flight calls via cancellation tokens or context propagation to free resources.
Complexity: O(m) tasks launched, each O(1) overhead; overall latency bounded by min(successTime, timeout). Space O(m) for task handles.

records.text: Merge two strings by longest suffix-prefix overlap. Category: Strings (OA, Sep 2026). Description: Try both orders, keep the larger overlap, prefer the original order on ties, linear time (prefix function).
key_points: Compute longest suffix‑prefix overlap using the KMP prefix function on (s2 + "#" + suffix_of_s1) for each order; O(|s1|+|s2|) time.
Run the overlap calculation twice (s1→s2 and s2→s1) and keep the larger overlap; on tie return the concatenation respecting original order.
Implementation steps: build combined string, compute prefix array, the last value gives overlap length.
Edge cases: no overlap (result is simple concatenation), full containment (one string is substring of the other), empty strings.
